messages:
rachel-peopleops: Heads up 1: new hire Jess (EAD pending) asked about traveling next month for consular stamping. She wants to know safe windows relative to start date + whether her pending EAD/receipt could cause issues.

omar-immigration: Short version: consulates vary. If Jess travels for a visa interview while an EAD is pending, bring the I-797C receipt, passport, any prior visa pages, and a letter from us summarizing employment and pending filing. We can prepare that letter.

jess-newhire: Thanks. My start date is May 10 and interview is currently scheduled for May 5. I worry about re-entry timing if stamping is delayed. Do we recommend postponing the interview?

rachel-peopleops: For payroll/benefits we need you at work on or before start date for new-hire orientation ideally. If travel risks missing start, we can shift orientation remotely for the first week but need final travel dates so we can document exceptions.

omar-immigration: If interview is before start and stamping likely quick, it's OK. But consulates sometimes issue administrative processing (weeks). If that happens you'd miss start. If the interview is close (<7 days) to start, safer to reschedule the consulate or push start. Also: if EAD eventually issues while you
re abroad there are complications re: returning on an EAD vs a stamped visa. Let's be cautious.

ben-sre: From an operational POV we also need a verified I-9. If your EAD isn't issued yet and you plan to use a visa to re-enter, ensure you bring visa paperwork and passport. We can do a remote document check, but Section 2 originals must be reviewed per policy within 3 business days of remote check.

jess-newhire: Ok got it. Is the one-page company summary enough for the consulate? What should it say?

omar-immigration: We'll include: (1) statement of offer, position title, start date, office location, (2) note that an EAD application is pending with receipt number, (3) contact info for immigration lead and HR, (4) request to consider the pending filing during adjudication. Keep it short and signed by HR. We'll draft and post here in a few hours.

rachel-peopleops: Also note benefits enrollment window: 30 days from start. If you miss start we can manually trigger a benefits exception but need advance notice. Please DM me travel itinerary so we can coordinate payroll/benefits.

imm-bot: Reminder set: "Draft consulate summary for Jess" in 2h.

jess-newhire: Thanks all. I'll attach my interview confirmation and passport scans here once booked. Please advise if you think rescheduling is smarter.

omar-immigration: If you want to play it safe, reschedule to after start or at least 10+ days before. But if you must keep the date, we'll prepare the letter and have HR flag payroll/benefits for a contingency.

rachel-peopleops: Agreed. Jess, ping when you have the confirmed appointment. We'll prepare the summary letter and set a concurrent remote-orientation plan if needed. :handshake:
